Title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - September 21, 2023
Overview: The Council opened with proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day, then heard extensive open comment and consent agenda items. The main actions were approving amendments to the Transit Village Area Plan (Boulder Junction Phase 2) and its Comprehensive Plan summary, and amending Ordinance 8599 on zoning for affordable and modest-size housing, with several changes deferred to phase two. The Council also discussed a letter endorsing county housing support, with a directive to bring a formal endorsement back later.

Topic1.Title: Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day Declarations
Topic1.Summary: Council presented a proclamation recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month from September 15 to October 15, with interpreters and community members speaking in Spanish and English. Council then presented an Energy Efficiency Day declaration for October 2023, urging residents to support clean energy goals.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic2.Summary: Eight in-person speakers and one virtual speaker addressed Council on topics including library building disposition, a Museum of Boulder exhibit, police monitor and homelessness near Central Park, architectural preservation, potty training facilities, a Landmarks Design Review Committee demolition, and a 28th and J housing project. Staff responded to several concerns, including the Central Park incident and the housing project.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-In
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3F unanimously by roll call. No council member called up the Life Sciences site review at 3825 Walnut Street, so it proceeded without a call-up.

Topic4.Title: Boulder Junction Phase 2 Transit Village Area Plan Amendments
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented amendments to the 2007 Transit Village Area Plan covering land use, transportation connections, and urban design for the Boulder Junction Phase 2 area. Council discussed mixed-use transit-oriented development versus mixed-use industrial zoning, anti-displacement strategies for small businesses, and retail sizing. Council approved both motions unanimously, including the staff recommendation not to add the planning board's office restriction.

Topic5.Title: Ordinance 8599: Zoning for Affordable and Modest-Size Housing
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented second reading amendments to the land use code to ease density, parking, and subdivision rules, aiming to increase middle housing and modest-size units. Council discussed site review exemptions, efficiency living unit use review, floor area bonuses, and rmx-1 rezoning, deferring several items to a future phase. Council amended and passed the ordinance unanimously, with a third reading expected as a consent item.

Topic6.Title: Letter to County Commissioners on Housing Ballot Measure
Topic6.Summary: Council member Benjamin proposed a letter to County Commissioners endorsing a proposed affordable and attainable housing tax, requesting investment in permanent supportive housing with wraparound services and transitional housing. Council generally supported sending the letter, with a formal endorsement resolution to follow through a future request.
